description: Run a paleontological investigation from site prospection through fossil preparation, taxonomic identification, taphonomic analysis, dating, and paleoenvironment reconstruction.

steps.description: Survey a region for fossil-bearing exposures, rank candidate sites by formation age, accessibility, and preservation potential.

inputs.name: target-region
inputs.desc: Geographic area and geologic formation to survey

inputs.name: target-taxa
inputs.desc: Taxa or time period of interest

inputs.name: access-constraints
inputs.desc: Land ownership, permits, seasonal access windows

outputs.name: candidate-sites
outputs.desc: Ranked list of prospection sites with GPS coordinates and formation data

outputs.name: permit-requirements
outputs.desc: Permits and landowner agreements needed per site

outputs.name: field-logistics
outputs.desc: Access routes, camp locations, water sources, and weather windows

process: Review published geologic maps and formation descriptions for the target region
Cross-reference known fossil localities in the Paleobiology Database with unexplored adjacent exposures
Rank each candidate by stratigraphic relevance, surface weathering rate, and logistical feasibility
Compile permit requirements and landowner contact information for top-ranked sites

steps.description: Design the excavation grid, assign quadrants, and define stratigraphic logging protocols for a fossil locality.

inputs.name: candidate-sites
inputs.desc: Selected site with GPS coordinates and formation data

inputs.name: target-taxa
inputs.desc: Taxa or morphological targets guiding excavation depth and extent

outputs.name: excavation-plan
outputs.desc: Grid layout with quadrant IDs, datum point, and dig sequence

outputs.name: strat-log-template
outputs.desc: Standardized stratigraphic logging sheet with lithology codes

outputs.name: collection-protocol
outputs.desc: Specimen numbering, GPS tagging, and field photography standards

process: Establish a permanent datum point and orient the grid to true north
Divide the exposure into 1-meter quadrants and assign unique IDs
Define vertical excavation intervals tied to lithologic changes
Set field numbering, photography, and GPS tagging standards for every specimen removed

steps.description: Stabilize, clean, and prepare fossil specimens for study using mechanical and chemical techniques appropriate to matrix type.

inputs.name: excavation-plan
inputs.desc: Grid and collection data for recovered specimens

inputs.name: matrix-type
inputs.desc: Lithology of enclosing sediment (sandstone, limestone, shale, etc.)

outputs.name: prepared-specimens
outputs.desc: Catalog of cleaned, stabilized specimens with preparation notes

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Methods, consolidants, and tools used per specimen

process: Assess each specimen for fragility, consolidant needs, and matrix hardness
Apply mechanical preparation (air scribe, pin vise) or chemical preparation (acetic acid, formic acid) as matrix dictates
Stabilize with appropriate consolidant (Paraloid B-72, cyanoacrylate) and document every application
Photograph each specimen at standard angles before and after preparation

steps.description: Identify prepared fossil specimens to the lowest possible taxonomic level using morphological comparison and published keys.

inputs.name: prepared-specimens
inputs.desc: Catalog of prepared specimens with photographs

inputs.name: target-taxa
inputs.desc: Expected taxonomic groups based on formation and age

outputs.name: taxonomic-assignments
outputs.desc: Each specimen assigned to order, family, genus, and species where possible

outputs.name: diagnostic-characters
outputs.desc: Key morphological features supporting each identification

outputs.name: unresolved-specimens
outputs.desc: Specimens requiring further comparison or CT scanning

process: Compare each specimen against published type descriptions and figured material
Score diagnostic morphological characters using a standardized character matrix
Flag specimens that fall outside known variation for the assigned taxon
Record confidence level (definite, probable, cf., aff.) for each assignment

steps.description: Analyze the preservation history of the fossil assemblage: transport, sorting, weathering, bioerosion, and burial conditions.

inputs.name: taxonomic-assignments
inputs.desc: Identified specimens with field context

inputs.name: strat-log-template
inputs.desc: Stratigraphic data from the excavation

outputs.name: taphonomic-report
outputs.desc: Assemblage-level taphonomic summary with preservation grades and transport indicators

outputs.name: depositional-interpretation
outputs.desc: Inferred depositional environment and burial history

process: Score each specimen for weathering stage, abrasion, bioerosion, and fragmentation
Map skeletal element representation and Voorhies Group ratios to assess transport sorting
Analyze spatial distribution within the grid for clustering, orientation, and dip patterns
Synthesize taphonomic signatures into a depositional and burial history narrative

steps.description: Select and justify the appropriate geochronological methods for dating the fossil-bearing horizon.

inputs.name: strat-log-template
inputs.desc: Stratigraphic column and lithology data

inputs.name: depositional-interpretation
inputs.desc: Depositional environment and mineralogy of the horizon

outputs.name: dating-plan
outputs.desc: Selected dating methods with sample requirements and expected precision

outputs.name: sample-collection-guide
outputs.desc: Instructions for collecting datable material from the section

process: Evaluate available datable materials: volcanic ash, detrital zircons, organic carbon, carbonate cement
Match each material to the best method (U-Pb, Ar-Ar, radiocarbon, magnetostratigraphy, biostratigraphy)
Estimate achievable precision and compare against the research question's temporal resolution needs
Write sampling protocol specifying collection method, contamination avoidance, and chain of custody

steps.description: Reconstruct the paleoenvironment of the fossil locality by integrating sedimentology, paleoecology, and geochemical proxies.

inputs.name: taphonomic-report
inputs.desc: Taphonomic signatures and depositional interpretation

inputs.name: taxonomic-assignments
inputs.desc: Faunal and floral list with abundance data

inputs.name: dating-plan
inputs.desc: Age constraints for the assemblage

outputs.name: paleoenvironment-model
outputs.desc: Reconstructed habitat, climate, and paleogeographic setting

outputs.name: site-summary-report
outputs.desc: Integrated report combining taxonomy, taphonomy, dating, and environment for publication

process: Identify paleoenvironmental indicator taxa and assess community structure
Integrate sedimentary facies analysis with stable isotope data where available
Compare the reconstructed environment with coeval localities in the region
Write the integrated site summary combining all analytical threads

description: Move a vaccine candidate from antigen selection through adjuvant screening, formulation, immunogenicity assay design, animal model protocol, correlate analysis, and regulatory pre-submission.

steps.description: Identify and rank candidate antigens based on conservation, immunodominance, expression level, and manufacturability.

inputs.name: pathogen-profile
inputs.desc: Target pathogen with genome or proteome reference

inputs.name: disease-epidemiology
inputs.desc: Incidence, mortality, and target population data

inputs.name: prior-candidates
inputs.desc: Any existing vaccine candidates or failed attempts for this pathogen

outputs.name: antigen-candidates
outputs.desc: Ranked list of antigens with conservation scores and expression feasibility

outputs.name: antigen-rationale
outputs.desc: Scientific justification for each candidate including immune evasion considerations

process: Screen the proteome for surface-exposed, conserved proteins across circulating strains
Score each candidate for predicted B-cell and T-cell epitope density
Assess manufacturability: expression system compatibility, solubility, stability, and scalability
Rank candidates by composite score and flag any with homology to human proteins

steps.description: Screen adjuvant candidates for compatibility with the selected antigen, measuring innate immune activation and formulation stability.

inputs.name: antigen-candidates
inputs.desc: Lead antigen candidates from selection step

inputs.name: target-immune-response
inputs.desc: Desired immune profile: Th1, Th2, mucosal, or balanced

outputs.name: adjuvant-shortlist
outputs.desc: Ranked adjuvants with compatibility and activation data

outputs.name: adjuvant-stability-data
outputs.desc: Accelerated stability results for antigen-adjuvant combinations

process: Compile candidate adjuvants matched to the desired immune polarization
Run in vitro innate activation assays (dendritic cell maturation, cytokine panel) for each combination
Measure antigen integrity after formulation with each adjuvant under accelerated stability conditions
Rank combinations by activation strength, antigen stability, and regulatory precedent

steps.description: Optimize the vaccine formulation for antigen dose, adjuvant ratio, buffer, and delivery format to maximize stability and immunogenicity.

inputs.name: antigen-candidates
inputs.desc: Lead antigen with expression and purification protocol

inputs.name: adjuvant-shortlist
inputs.desc: Top adjuvant candidates with compatibility data

outputs.name: optimized-formulation
outputs.desc: Final formulation with dose, ratio, buffer, pH, and storage conditions

outputs.name: formulation-stability-report
outputs.desc: Real-time and accelerated stability data for the final formulation

process: Design a dose-response matrix crossing antigen concentration with adjuvant ratio
Screen buffer and pH combinations for particle size, zeta potential, and antigen adsorption
Run accelerated stability (25C/60%RH and 40C/75%RH) and freeze-thaw cycling
Select the formulation that maximizes stability window while staying within manufacturing constraints

steps.description: Design the immunogenicity assay panel to measure humoral and cellular immune responses in preclinical and clinical samples.

inputs.name: optimized-formulation
inputs.desc: Final vaccine formulation with expected immune targets

inputs.name: target-immune-response
inputs.desc: Desired immune profile guiding assay selection

outputs.name: assay-panel
outputs.desc: List of assays (ELISA, neutralization, ELISpot, flow cytometry) with SOPs and acceptance criteria

outputs.name: reagent-requirements
outputs.desc: Reagent sourcing, reference standards, and positive controls needed

process: Select binding antibody assays (ELISA) and functional assays (neutralization, opsonophagocytosis) for humoral response
Select T-cell assays (ELISpot, intracellular cytokine staining) for cellular response
Define assay acceptance criteria, positive/negative controls, and reportable range
Write SOPs with plate layouts, reagent concentrations, and data analysis methods

steps.description: Design the preclinical animal study protocol including species selection, group sizes, dosing schedule, sample collection, and endpoints.

inputs.name: optimized-formulation
inputs.desc: Final vaccine formulation to be tested

inputs.name: assay-panel
inputs.desc: Immunogenicity assays that will be run on collected samples

outputs.name: animal-protocol
outputs.desc: Complete study protocol with species, groups, schedule, and endpoints

outputs.name: ethics-submission
outputs.desc: IACUC or equivalent ethics committee submission package

process: Select animal model based on pathogen susceptibility, immune system relevance, and regulatory guidance
Calculate group sizes using power analysis for the primary immunogenicity endpoint
Design the dosing and sampling schedule with prime, boost, and challenge timepoints
Prepare the ethics submission with humane endpoints, housing, and veterinary oversight plan

steps.description: Analyze preclinical immunogenicity and challenge data to identify correlates of protection and define the target product profile.

inputs.name: animal-protocol
inputs.desc: Study design for reference

inputs.name: assay-panel
inputs.desc: Assays used to measure immune response

outputs.name: correlate-analysis
outputs.desc: Statistical analysis linking immune markers to protection outcomes

outputs.name: target-product-profile
outputs.desc: Minimum and preferred immune response thresholds for efficacy

process: Tabulate individual-animal immune responses against protection outcomes (survival, viral load, pathology score)
Run receiver operating characteristic analysis to identify threshold values for each immune marker
Test multivariate models combining humoral and cellular markers for predictive accuracy
Define the target product profile with minimum protective immune response benchmarks

steps.description: Assemble the regulatory pre-submission dossier (pre-IND or scientific advice) with CMC, nonclinical, and proposed clinical sections.

inputs.name: optimized-formulation
inputs.desc: CMC data for the vaccine formulation

inputs.name: correlate-analysis
inputs.desc: Preclinical efficacy and correlate data

inputs.name: target-product-profile
inputs.desc: Proposed TPP with immune response thresholds

outputs.name: pre-submission-dossier
outputs.desc: Complete pre-IND or scientific advice briefing document

outputs.name: regulatory-questions
outputs.desc: Specific questions for the agency meeting agenda

process: Compile CMC section: manufacturing process, analytical methods, stability, and specifications
Compile nonclinical section: toxicology, immunogenicity, challenge study results, and correlate analysis
Draft proposed Phase 1 clinical design: population, dose escalation, endpoints, and stopping rules
Format the briefing document per agency template and draft the meeting request with key questions

description: Investigate a microbial isolate from strain isolation through growth characterization, susceptibility testing, biofilm assay, metabolic profiling, genomic annotation, and resistance reporting.

steps.description: Isolate a pure microbial strain from a mixed sample using selective media, colony morphology, and confirmatory identification.

inputs.name: sample-source
inputs.desc: Origin of the sample (clinical, environmental, food, etc.)

inputs.name: target-organism
inputs.desc: Suspected organism or group to isolate

inputs.name: biosafety-level
inputs.desc: Required BSL and containment procedures

outputs.name: pure-isolate
outputs.desc: Confirmed pure culture with strain ID and cryostock location

outputs.name: isolation-record
outputs.desc: Media used, colony morphology, Gram stain, and confirmatory test results

process: Plate sample on selective and differential media appropriate for the target group
Pick isolated colonies and streak for purity through three successive passages
Confirm identity by Gram stain, catalase/oxidase, and 16S rRNA sequencing or MALDI-TOF
Prepare glycerol cryostocks at -80C and record strain provenance in the lab database

steps.description: Characterize the growth kinetics of an isolate across conditions to determine lag, exponential, and stationary phase parameters.

inputs.name: pure-isolate
inputs.desc: Confirmed pure culture to characterize

inputs.name: growth-conditions
inputs.desc: Temperature, atmosphere, and media variations to test

outputs.name: growth-curves
outputs.desc: OD600 time series with fitted lag time, doubling time, and max OD for each condition

outputs.name: optimal-conditions
outputs.desc: Condition yielding the fastest exponential growth and highest yield

process: Inoculate standardized starter cultures and normalize to a fixed OD600
Measure OD600 at regular intervals across all condition combinations in triplicate
Fit the Baranyi or Gompertz growth model to extract lag, rate, and asymptote parameters
Identify the optimal condition set for downstream assays

steps.description: Determine the antimicrobial susceptibility profile of the isolate using broth microdilution or disk diffusion per CLSI standards.

inputs.name: pure-isolate
inputs.desc: Pure culture at known density

inputs.name: antibiotic-panel
inputs.desc: Antibiotics and concentration ranges to test

outputs.name: susceptibility-profile
outputs.desc: MIC values and S/I/R interpretation for each antibiotic

outputs.name: resistance-flags
outputs.desc: Phenotypic resistance patterns warranting further investigation

process: Prepare inoculum to 0.5 McFarland standard and distribute into broth microdilution plates
Incubate for 16-20 hours and read MIC as the lowest concentration with no visible growth
Interpret MIC values against CLSI breakpoints for the organism and antibiotic
Flag multidrug resistance patterns and inducible resistance phenotypes for genomic follow-up

steps.description: Quantify biofilm formation capacity using crystal violet staining and confocal microscopy to assess clinical or environmental persistence risk.

inputs.name: pure-isolate
inputs.desc: Pure culture to assess for biofilm formation

inputs.name: optimal-conditions
inputs.desc: Growth conditions optimized in earlier step

outputs.name: biofilm-quantification
outputs.desc: Crystal violet OD measurements with strong/moderate/weak/none classification

outputs.name: biofilm-images
outputs.desc: Confocal z-stack images showing biofilm architecture

process: Grow the isolate in 96-well polystyrene plates under static conditions for 24 and 48 hours
Wash, fix, and stain adherent biomass with crystal violet, then solubilize and measure OD570
Classify biofilm capacity against reference strain controls
Image representative wells by confocal laser scanning microscopy with live/dead staining

steps.description: Profile the metabolic capabilities of the isolate using Biolog phenotype arrays or targeted substrate utilization panels.

inputs.name: pure-isolate
inputs.desc: Pure culture for metabolic characterization

inputs.name: growth-curves
inputs.desc: Growth parameters informing incubation time

outputs.name: metabolic-profile
outputs.desc: Substrate utilization matrix with positive, negative, and weak reactions

outputs.name: metabolic-cluster
outputs.desc: Comparison to reference profiles for phenotypic species confirmation

process: Inoculate Biolog GEN III or equivalent phenotype microarray per manufacturer protocol
Read kinetically or at endpoint and score each well as positive, borderline, or negative
Compare the utilization pattern against the database for species-level confirmation
Identify unusual metabolic capabilities that may explain niche adaptation

steps.description: Assemble, annotate, and analyze the whole genome sequence of the isolate to identify virulence factors, resistance genes, and mobile elements.

inputs.name: pure-isolate
inputs.desc: DNA extracted from the pure culture

inputs.name: resistance-flags
inputs.desc: Phenotypic resistance patterns to confirm genotypically

outputs.name: annotated-genome
outputs.desc: Assembled and annotated genome with gene coordinates and functional assignments

outputs.name: resistance-genotype
outputs.desc: Identified resistance genes, their genetic context, and mobile element associations

outputs.name: virulence-inventory
outputs.desc: Virulence factors, secretion systems, and pathogenicity islands identified

process: Assemble reads using a hybrid (short + long read) or short-read-only pipeline
Annotate with Prokka or PGAP and screen against CARD, VFDB, and ISfinder databases
Map resistance genes to mobile elements (plasmids, transposons, integrons) using Abricate and MOB-suite
Compare the genome to the closest reference strain and report unique or missing gene content

steps.description: Synthesize phenotypic and genomic findings into a resistance mechanism report linking genotype to observed phenotype.

inputs.name: susceptibility-profile
inputs.desc: MIC values and resistance phenotype

inputs.name: resistance-genotype
inputs.desc: Resistance genes and their genomic context

inputs.name: virulence-inventory
inputs.desc: Virulence factor data for clinical context

outputs.name: resistance-report
outputs.desc: Integrated report mapping each resistance phenotype to its genetic determinant

outputs.name: clinical-implications
outputs.desc: Treatment recommendations and infection control notes based on resistance profile

process: Align each phenotypic resistance to its candidate gene(s) and assess concordance
Flag discordant results (phenotype without known gene, or gene without phenotype) for follow-up
Assess horizontal transfer risk based on mobile element context
Write the summary report with treatment implications and recommended infection control measures

description: Run a seismological investigation from station layout through waveform processing, event detection, magnitude estimation, focal mechanism, attenuation modeling, and hazard assessment.

steps.description: Design a seismic station network for a target region, optimizing station spacing, site selection, and data telemetry for detection threshold goals.

inputs.name: target-region
inputs.desc: Geographic bounds and tectonic setting of the study area

inputs.name: detection-threshold
inputs.desc: Minimum magnitude the network must detect and locate

inputs.name: existing-stations
inputs.desc: Inventory of existing seismic stations in and near the region

outputs.name: network-design
outputs.desc: Station coordinates, sensor types, and telemetry plan

outputs.name: detection-capability
outputs.desc: Modeled detection and location thresholds across the network footprint

process: Model detection thresholds for the existing network using ambient noise levels and path attenuation
Identify coverage gaps where the detection threshold exceeds the target magnitude
Place new stations to close gaps, balancing azimuthal coverage against site accessibility
Specify sensor type (broadband, short-period, accelerometer) and telemetry (cellular, satellite, radio) per site

steps.description: Process raw seismic waveforms: instrument response removal, filtering, and quality control to produce analysis-ready traces.

inputs.name: network-design
inputs.desc: Station metadata (coordinates, sensor response, orientation)

inputs.name: raw-waveforms
inputs.desc: Continuous or triggered waveform data in miniSEED or equivalent

outputs.name: processed-traces
outputs.desc: Instrument-corrected, filtered, QC-passed waveforms in standard format

outputs.name: data-quality-log
outputs.desc: Gaps, noise anomalies, and timing issues flagged per station-day

process: Remove instrument response to convert counts to ground velocity or acceleration
Apply bandpass filter appropriate for the target magnitude range
Flag and log data gaps, timing jumps, and noise anomalies
Output analysis-ready traces with updated metadata headers

steps.description: Detect and locate seismic events from processed waveforms using automated picking, association, and location algorithms.

inputs.name: processed-traces
inputs.desc: QC-passed waveforms for the analysis period

inputs.name: velocity-model
inputs.desc: 1D or 3D velocity model for the study region

outputs.name: event-catalog
outputs.desc: List of detected events with origin time, latitude, longitude, depth, and phase picks

outputs.name: location-uncertainties
outputs.desc: Formal error ellipses and RMS residuals for each event

process: Run STA/LTA or deep-learning phase picker on all station traces
Associate picks into events using travel-time consistency checks
Locate each event by iterative least-squares inversion against the velocity model
Filter the catalog by minimum phase count and maximum RMS residual

steps.description: Estimate event magnitudes (local, moment, duration) for each cataloged event and assess magnitude completeness of the catalog.

inputs.name: event-catalog
inputs.desc: Located events with phase picks and waveform associations

inputs.name: processed-traces
inputs.desc: Waveforms for amplitude and spectral measurements

outputs.name: magnitude-catalog
outputs.desc: Events with ML, Mw, or Md estimates and station magnitudes

outputs.name: completeness-analysis
outputs.desc: Magnitude of completeness (Mc) and Gutenberg-Richter b-value for the catalog

process: Measure peak amplitudes and compute local magnitude (ML) with path and station corrections
Compute moment magnitude (Mw) from spectral fitting where signal-to-noise allows
Estimate magnitude of completeness using the maximum curvature method
Fit the Gutenberg-Richter frequency-magnitude relation and report the b-value

steps.description: Determine earthquake focal mechanisms (fault plane solutions) from P-wave first motions or moment tensor inversion.

inputs.name: event-catalog
inputs.desc: Located events for mechanism analysis

inputs.name: processed-traces
inputs.desc: Broadband waveforms for moment tensor inversion

outputs.name: focal-mechanisms
outputs.desc: Beach ball plots with strike, dip, and rake for each solved event

outputs.name: stress-field-indicators
outputs.desc: Principal stress orientations inferred from mechanism population

process: Pick P-wave first motion polarities at each station for well-recorded events
Solve the fault plane solution by grid search over the focal sphere
For larger events, run full waveform moment tensor inversion
Invert the mechanism population for regional stress tensor orientation

steps.description: Model seismic wave attenuation (Q) for the study region to support ground motion prediction and hazard calculations.

inputs.name: magnitude-catalog
inputs.desc: Events with magnitudes and station data

inputs.name: processed-traces
inputs.desc: Waveforms for spectral decay measurement

outputs.name: attenuation-model
outputs.desc: Frequency-dependent Q model and geometric spreading function for the region

outputs.name: site-amplification
outputs.desc: Site response estimates (Vs30-based or H/V ratio) for each station

process: Measure spectral amplitudes at multiple distances for a set of reference events
Invert for path attenuation (Q) and site amplification simultaneously
Validate the Q model by comparing predicted and observed spectral amplitudes for an independent event set
Estimate site amplification at each station from Vs30 proxies or horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratios

steps.description: Compute probabilistic seismic hazard for the study region by combining source models, ground motion models, and site effects.

inputs.name: magnitude-catalog
inputs.desc: Catalog with completeness and b-value parameters

inputs.name: focal-mechanisms
inputs.desc: Fault characterization data

inputs.name: attenuation-model
inputs.desc: Regional attenuation and site amplification

outputs.name: hazard-curves
outputs.desc: Annual exceedance probability curves for PGA and spectral accelerations at key periods

outputs.name: hazard-map
outputs.desc: Gridded hazard map for the target return periods (475-year, 2475-year)

process: Build seismic source models: area sources, fault sources, and smoothed seismicity
Assign ground motion prediction equations calibrated to the regional attenuation model
Run probabilistic seismic hazard analysis using OpenQuake or equivalent engine
Generate hazard curves and uniform hazard spectra at target sites and gridded hazard maps

description: Run a plant science field trial from germplasm selection through plot design, growth monitoring, phenotype scoring, yield analysis, statistical reporting, and seed bank accession.

steps.description: Select germplasm entries for a field trial by screening available accessions against target traits, adaptation zone, and trial objectives.

inputs.name: trial-objective
inputs.desc: Breeding objective: yield, disease resistance, quality, stress tolerance, etc.

inputs.name: adaptation-zone
inputs.desc: Climate, soil type, and latitude of the trial site

inputs.name: available-accessions
inputs.desc: Germplasm collection or seed catalog to screen

outputs.name: selected-entries
outputs.desc: List of accessions chosen for the trial with pedigree and trait data

outputs.name: check-varieties
outputs.desc: Reference varieties serving as controls

process: Filter accessions by adaptation zone, maturity group, and availability of sufficient seed
Rank candidates by prior performance data for the target trait
Select check varieties representing the current commercial standard and a known susceptible control
Confirm seed quantity and viability for all selected entries

steps.description: Design the field layout with appropriate experimental design (RCBD, alpha-lattice, augmented) and generate the randomization plan.

inputs.name: selected-entries
inputs.desc: Entries and checks to include in the trial

inputs.name: field-dimensions
inputs.desc: Available field area, row spacing, and plot size constraints

outputs.name: randomization-plan
outputs.desc: Plot map with entry assignments, replicate structure, and blocking

outputs.name: planting-guide
outputs.desc: Row-by-row planting sequence with seed amounts per plot

process: Select experimental design based on entry count and field heterogeneity (RCBD for <30, alpha-lattice for larger)
Generate randomization with appropriate blocking and guard rows
Produce the plot map with GPS coordinates for each plot corner
Calculate seed requirements per plot including a 10% buffer

steps.description: Monitor and record growth conditions throughout the trial: soil moisture, temperature, rainfall, and pest or disease pressure.

inputs.name: randomization-plan
inputs.desc: Plot map for georeferencing observation points

inputs.name: monitoring-schedule
inputs.desc: Frequency and timing of observations (weekly, phenological stage)

outputs.name: environment-log
outputs.desc: Time series of temperature, rainfall, soil moisture, and growing degree days

outputs.name: stress-events
outputs.desc: Dated records of drought, flood, frost, pest outbreak, or disease incidence

process: Install or confirm weather station and soil moisture sensors at the trial site
Record daily weather and compute cumulative growing degree days
Scout for pest and disease incidence on the prescribed schedule and record severity ratings
Flag stress events that may require covariate adjustment in the analysis

steps.description: Score phenotypic traits at defined growth stages using standardized scales for morphology, disease resistance, and agronomic performance.

inputs.name: selected-entries
inputs.desc: Entries being evaluated with their target traits

inputs.name: randomization-plan
inputs.desc: Plot map for systematic scoring order

outputs.name: phenotype-data
outputs.desc: Scored trait values per plot per scoring date

outputs.name: scoring-notes
outputs.desc: Observer notes on off-types, lodging, bird damage, or border effects

process: Define the trait list, scoring scale, and growth stage for each observation
Train scorers on the scale with reference photographs and calibration plots
Score plots in serpentine order within each replicate to minimize environmental trend bias
Enter data same-day and run range checks to catch transcription errors

steps.description: Harvest, weigh, and analyze yield components (grain weight, biomass, harvest index) with moisture correction.

inputs.name: randomization-plan
inputs.desc: Plot map and harvest area per plot

inputs.name: phenotype-data
inputs.desc: Maturity and lodging data informing harvest timing

outputs.name: yield-data
outputs.desc: Plot yields corrected to standard moisture with yield components

outputs.name: harvest-quality
outputs.desc: Test weight, protein, or other quality parameters

process: Harvest the net plot area at physiological maturity, excluding border rows
Weigh grain and biomass, measure moisture, and correct to standard moisture content
Subsample for yield components: thousand kernel weight, kernels per spike, spikes per area
Measure quality parameters (test weight, protein, oil) on a subsample per plot

steps.description: Analyze the trial data using mixed models, compute entry means, heritability, and genetic gain, and produce the trial report.

inputs.name: yield-data
inputs.desc: Plot-level yield and yield component data

inputs.name: phenotype-data
inputs.desc: All scored trait data

inputs.name: environment-log
inputs.desc: Environmental covariates for the growing season

outputs.name: trial-report
outputs.desc: Statistical summary with entry means, LSD, heritability, and genetic gain estimates

outputs.name: selection-recommendations
outputs.desc: Entries recommended for advancement, discard, or retesting

process: Fit a mixed model with entry as fixed or random, replicate and block as random
Estimate entry means (BLUPs or BLUEs), LSD, and broad-sense heritability
Calculate predicted genetic gain for the selection intensity applied
Rank entries and flag those exceeding the check mean for advancement

steps.description: Process and deposit seed from selected entries into a seed bank with full passport data and viability testing.

inputs.name: selection-recommendations
inputs.desc: Entries selected for advancement or conservation

inputs.name: yield-data
inputs.desc: Harvest data including seed lot origin

outputs.name: accession-records
outputs.desc: Seed bank accession numbers with passport data (origin, pedigree, traits)

outputs.name: viability-test
outputs.desc: Germination test results for each deposited lot

process: Clean and dry seed lots to target moisture content for long-term storage
Run a standard germination test (ISTA rules) and record percent germination
Package seed in moisture-barrier containers and deposit at the designated storage temperature
Enter passport data (accession number, species, pedigree, collection site, trait summary) into the genebank database

description: Plan and execute an atmospheric measurement campaign from instrument deployment through radiosonde launches, remote sensing calibration, boundary layer profiling, trajectory analysis, and chemical transport modeling.

steps.description: Plan the instrument suite and site layout for a field campaign, including power, data logging, and maintenance schedules.

inputs.name: campaign-objectives
inputs.desc: Scientific questions driving the measurement campaign

inputs.name: site-characteristics
inputs.desc: Geography, land use, elevation, and access at the field site

inputs.name: measurement-period
inputs.desc: Start date, end date, and intensive observation windows

outputs.name: instrument-plan
outputs.desc: Instrument list with specifications, placement coordinates, and data logging configuration

outputs.name: maintenance-schedule
outputs.desc: Calibration check and consumable replacement timeline

process: Map campaign objectives to required measurements (radiation, winds, temperature, humidity, trace gases, aerosols)
Select instruments and specify placement to minimize interference and maximize fetch
Design power supply (mains, solar, generator) and data acquisition system with backup logging
Schedule pre-deployment calibration, mid-campaign checks, and post-campaign calibration

steps.description: Design the radiosonde launch schedule to capture diurnal boundary layer evolution, synoptic transitions, and special event triggers.

inputs.name: campaign-objectives
inputs.desc: Vertical profiling requirements

inputs.name: measurement-period
inputs.desc: Campaign dates and intensive observation periods

outputs.name: launch-schedule
outputs.desc: Calendar of launches with times, balloon specs, and payload configuration

outputs.name: launch-sop
outputs.desc: Standard operating procedure for sonde preparation, inflation, release, and data QC

process: Set baseline launch times to match WMO synoptic hours (00Z, 12Z) plus dawn/dusk for boundary layer transitions
Add intensive observation period launches at 3-hour intervals during target meteorological events
Define event-triggered launches (thunderstorm approach, frontal passage, pollution episode)
Write the launch SOP covering sonde activation, surface check, inflation, release criteria, and real-time data QC

steps.description: Calibrate ground-based remote sensing instruments (lidar, ceilometer, radiometer, sodar) against radiosonde truth and maintain traceability.

inputs.name: instrument-plan
inputs.desc: Remote sensing instruments deployed at the site

inputs.name: launch-schedule
inputs.desc: Radiosonde launches providing calibration truth

outputs.name: calibration-report
outputs.desc: Bias, RMSE, and correlation against sonde truth for each instrument and variable

outputs.name: correction-factors
outputs.desc: Empirical corrections to apply to continuous remote sensing retrievals

process: Co-locate radiosonde profiles with simultaneous remote sensing retrievals at matching heights
Compute bias, RMSE, and Pearson correlation for temperature, humidity, and wind speed profiles
Derive height-dependent correction factors and assess their stability across weather regimes
Document calibration traceability chain from reference standard to field measurement

steps.description: Diagnose atmospheric boundary layer height, structure, and turbulence from combined surface, profile, and remote sensing data.

inputs.name: calibration-report
inputs.desc: Calibrated remote sensing data streams

inputs.name: instrument-plan
inputs.desc: Surface flux and turbulence measurements available

outputs.name: boundary-layer-heights
outputs.desc: Time series of diagnosed BL height with method and confidence flag

outputs.name: turbulence-profiles
outputs.desc: Vertical profiles of turbulent kinetic energy, heat flux, and moisture flux

process: Apply multiple BL height detection methods (gradient, parcel, Richardson number) to each sonde and lidar profile
Reconcile methods into a best-estimate BL height time series with uncertainty bounds
Compute turbulence statistics from sonic anemometer data and diagnose stability class (Monin-Obukhov)
Build composite diurnal cycles of BL height, entrainment zone thickness, and residual layer structure

steps.description: Compute backward and forward air mass trajectories to identify source regions and transport pathways for observed pollutants or meteorological events.

inputs.name: boundary-layer-heights
inputs.desc: BL height data to set trajectory arrival heights

inputs.name: measurement-period
inputs.desc: Dates and times of interest for trajectory computation

outputs.name: trajectory-ensemble
outputs.desc: Multi-height, multi-model trajectory sets with source region classification

outputs.name: source-attribution
outputs.desc: Probability maps of source region contribution based on trajectory density and residence time

process: Run HYSPLIT or FLEXPART backward trajectories at multiple arrival heights within and above the BL
Classify trajectory clusters by source region using geographic or land-use masks
Compute concentration-weighted trajectory (CWT) or potential source contribution function (PSCF) maps
Cross-reference high-pollution events with trajectory clusters to attribute source regions

steps.description: Configure and run a chemical transport model for the campaign domain to simulate pollutant formation, transport, and deposition.

inputs.name: source-attribution
inputs.desc: Emission source regions identified from trajectory analysis

inputs.name: boundary-layer-heights
inputs.desc: Observed BL heights for model evaluation

outputs.name: model-output
outputs.desc: Simulated concentration fields for target species over the campaign period

outputs.name: model-evaluation
outputs.desc: Bias, RMSE, and correlation of simulated vs. observed concentrations at the field site

process: Configure the model domain, resolution, meteorological driver, and emission inventory
Run the chemical transport simulation for the campaign period with hourly output
Extract model values at the field site location and compare against surface and profile observations
Diagnose model biases by time of day, wind direction, and chemical regime

steps.description: Synthesize all campaign datasets into a summary report documenting key findings, data quality, and recommendations for follow-up.

inputs.name: model-evaluation
inputs.desc: Model performance against observations

inputs.name: source-attribution
inputs.desc: Source region analysis results

inputs.name: boundary-layer-heights
inputs.desc: BL structure and turbulence findings

outputs.name: campaign-report
outputs.desc: Integrated campaign summary with key findings, data inventory, and quality flags

outputs.name: data-archive-manifest
outputs.desc: File inventory, formats, and metadata for archival in a public repository

process: Summarize the meteorological context of the campaign period relative to climatology
Highlight the key scientific findings supported by the observational and modeling evidence
Document data quality, known issues, and recommended corrections for each instrument
Prepare the data archive with standardized file formats, metadata, and DOI registration

description: Develop a polymer from monomer selection through polymerization design, molecular weight and thermal characterization, mechanical testing, aging study, and application suitability report.

steps.description: Select monomers based on target polymer properties, assess sourcing options, and confirm purity specifications.

inputs.name: target-properties
inputs.desc: Desired mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties of the final polymer

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: End-use environment: temperature range, chemical exposure, regulatory constraints

outputs.name: monomer-candidates
outputs.desc: Ranked monomer list with structure, supplier, purity, and cost

outputs.name: copolymer-ratios
outputs.desc: Proposed comonomer ratios if a copolymer strategy is needed

process: Map target properties to polymer backbone and side-chain requirements
Identify candidate monomers and rank by property match, availability, and cost
Evaluate copolymerization options if a single monomer cannot meet all property targets
Confirm supplier purity specs and order sufficient material for screening and scale-up

steps.description: Design the polymerization reaction: mechanism, initiator, solvent, temperature profile, and target conversion.

inputs.name: monomer-candidates
inputs.desc: Selected monomers with purity and reactivity data

inputs.name: copolymer-ratios
inputs.desc: Comonomer feed ratios if applicable

outputs.name: reaction-protocol
outputs.desc: Step-by-step synthesis protocol with reagent quantities, conditions, and safety notes

outputs.name: conversion-targets
outputs.desc: Target conversion, molecular weight, and dispersity

process: Select polymerization mechanism (free radical, ATRP, RAFT, ring-opening, condensation) based on monomer chemistry
Choose initiator, catalyst, and solvent system with rationale
Design the temperature and feed profile to control molecular weight and dispersity
Write the bench-scale synthesis protocol with safety data sheet references

steps.description: Measure molecular weight distribution by GPC/SEC and confirm structure by NMR and FTIR.

inputs.name: reaction-protocol
inputs.desc: Synthesis conditions for the batch being characterized

inputs.name: conversion-targets
inputs.desc: Expected Mn, Mw, and dispersity

outputs.name: mw-distribution
outputs.desc: Mn, Mw, dispersity, and full MWD curve from GPC

outputs.name: structural-confirmation
outputs.desc: NMR and FTIR spectra confirming monomer incorporation and end groups

process: Dissolve polymer in GPC-grade solvent and run against narrow-standard calibration
Record Mn, Mw, Mz, and dispersity from the chromatogram
Acquire 1H-NMR to confirm repeat unit structure and estimate end-group composition
Collect FTIR spectrum and assign key functional group absorptions

steps.description: Characterize thermal transitions (Tg, Tm, Td) by DSC and TGA to define processing and service temperature windows.

inputs.name: mw-distribution
inputs.desc: Molecular weight data for the sample

inputs.name: target-properties
inputs.desc: Required service temperature range

outputs.name: thermal-properties
outputs.desc: Glass transition (Tg), melting point (Tm), crystallinity, and decomposition onset (Td)

outputs.name: processing-window
outputs.desc: Recommended processing temperature range based on thermal data

process: Run DSC with heat-cool-heat cycle to erase thermal history and identify Tg and Tm
Calculate percent crystallinity from the melting enthalpy against 100% crystalline reference
Run TGA from ambient to 600C to determine decomposition onset and char yield
Define the processing window between Tm (or Tg + 100C for amorphous) and Td

steps.description: Test mechanical properties (tensile, flexural, impact) of molded specimens according to ASTM or ISO standards.

inputs.name: processing-window
inputs.desc: Molding conditions derived from thermal analysis

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: Mechanical performance targets for the end use

outputs.name: mechanical-data
outputs.desc: Tensile modulus, yield strength, elongation at break, flexural modulus, and impact strength

outputs.name: stress-strain-curves
outputs.desc: Full stress-strain curves for each specimen set

process: Mold test specimens (dogbones, bars) at the specified processing conditions
Condition specimens at 23C/50% RH for 48 hours per ASTM D618
Run tensile (ASTM D638), flexural (ASTM D790), and impact (ASTM D256) tests at n >= 5 per condition
Calculate mean, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation for each property

steps.description: Subject polymer specimens to accelerated aging (thermal, UV, hydrolytic) and track property retention over time.

inputs.name: mechanical-data
inputs.desc: Baseline mechanical properties for comparison

inputs.name: application-requirements
inputs.desc: Service environment: temperature, UV exposure, humidity, chemical contact

outputs.name: aging-curves
outputs.desc: Property retention vs. aging time for each degradation mode

outputs.name: lifetime-estimate
outputs.desc: Projected service lifetime using Arrhenius or time-temperature superposition

process: Expose specimen sets to accelerated conditions: 85C/85%RH thermal, UV-A 340nm, or immersion
Pull specimens at defined intervals and remeasure mechanical properties and molecular weight
Plot property retention curves and identify the failure threshold
Apply Arrhenius extrapolation or time-temperature superposition to estimate real-world service life

steps.description: Compile all characterization data into a suitability report evaluating the polymer against the original application requirements.

inputs.name: mechanical-data
inputs.desc: Baseline mechanical properties

inputs.name: thermal-properties
inputs.desc: Thermal transition and stability data

inputs.name: aging-curves
inputs.desc: Property retention under accelerated aging

outputs.name: suitability-report
outputs.desc: Pass/fail assessment per requirement with supporting data and recommendations

outputs.name: scale-up-notes
outputs.desc: Process adjustments needed for pilot or production scale

process: Tabulate each application requirement against measured property values
Score pass/marginal/fail for each requirement with the supporting data reference
Identify any property gaps and propose formulation or compounding modifications
Outline scale-up considerations: reactor size, mixing, cooling, and quality control points

description: Run a bioinformatics analysis from raw sequence QC through alignment, variant calling or differential expression, pathway enrichment, network construction, visualization, and reproducible documentation.

steps.description: Assess raw sequencing read quality, trim adapters and low-quality bases, and filter contamination.

inputs.name: raw-reads
inputs.desc: FASTQ files from the sequencing platform

inputs.name: sequencing-metadata
inputs.desc: Platform, library prep, read length, and expected coverage

outputs.name: trimmed-reads
outputs.desc: Adapter-trimmed, quality-filtered FASTQ files

outputs.name: qc-report
outputs.desc: FastQC and MultiQC summary of per-base quality, GC content, duplication, and adapter content

process: Run FastQC on raw reads and inspect per-base quality, adapter content, and overrepresented sequences
Trim adapters and low-quality tails with Trimmomatic, fastp, or cutadapt
Screen for contaminant sequences (host, PhiX, vectors) with Kraken2 or BBTools
Re-run FastQC on trimmed reads and compile MultiQC report

steps.description: Align trimmed reads to a reference genome or transcriptome and generate sorted, deduplicated BAM files.

inputs.name: trimmed-reads
inputs.desc: Quality-filtered FASTQ files

inputs.name: reference-genome
inputs.desc: Reference genome or transcriptome FASTA with index

outputs.name: aligned-bam
outputs.desc: Sorted, indexed, deduplicated BAM files per sample

outputs.name: alignment-stats
outputs.desc: Mapping rate, duplication rate, insert size, and coverage per sample

process: Index the reference genome if not already indexed
Align reads with BWA-MEM2 (DNA) or STAR/HISAT2 (RNA) using default or tuned parameters
Sort by coordinate, mark duplicates with Picard or samblaster, and index the BAM
Collect alignment statistics with samtools stats and Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics

steps.description: Call variants (DNA) or quantify differential expression (RNA) depending on the experiment type.

inputs.name: aligned-bam
inputs.desc: Sorted, deduplicated BAM files per sample

inputs.name: experiment-design
inputs.desc: Sample groups, contrasts, and analysis type (variant calling or DGE)

outputs.name: call-results
outputs.desc: VCF of called variants (DNA) or table of differentially expressed genes with fold change and adjusted p-value (RNA)

outputs.name: call-qc
outputs.desc: Ti/Tv ratio, variant type distribution (DNA) or dispersion estimates, MA plot (RNA)

process: For DNA: call variants with GATK HaplotypeCaller or DeepVariant, filter with VQSR or hard filters
For RNA: quantify gene counts with featureCounts or Salmon, run DESeq2 or edgeR for differential expression
Apply multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg) and set significance thresholds
Generate QC plots: Ti/Tv and variant summary (DNA) or MA plot and dispersion (RNA)

steps.description: Test gene lists or ranked gene sets against pathway and ontology databases to identify enriched biological processes.

inputs.name: call-results
inputs.desc: Significant variants (DNA) or differentially expressed genes (RNA)

inputs.name: organism-annotation
inputs.desc: Species and gene annotation database (GO, KEGG, Reactome)

outputs.name: enrichment-results
outputs.desc: Enriched pathways and GO terms with p-values, FDR, and gene lists

outputs.name: pathway-summary
outputs.desc: Top enriched processes grouped by biological theme

process: Run over-representation analysis (ORA) on the significant gene set against GO and KEGG
Run gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on the full ranked gene list for unbiased discovery
Correct for multiple testing and filter by FDR < 0.05
Group enriched terms by biological theme to reduce redundancy (REVIGO or simplifyEnrichment)

steps.description: Build protein-protein interaction or gene co-expression networks from the enriched gene sets and identify functional modules.

inputs.name: enrichment-results
inputs.desc: Enriched gene sets for network seeding

inputs.name: call-results
inputs.desc: Full expression or variant data for edge weighting

outputs.name: network-graph
outputs.desc: Node and edge table for the constructed network with module assignments

outputs.name: hub-genes
outputs.desc: Top hub and bottleneck genes ranked by centrality measures

process: Query STRING or BioGRID for known interactions among the enriched gene set
Add co-expression edges from WGCNA or correlation analysis if expression data is available
Detect functional modules using Louvain or MCL clustering
Rank nodes by degree, betweenness, and closeness centrality to identify hub genes

steps.description: Create publication-quality figures: volcano plots, heatmaps, network diagrams, and pathway maps.

inputs.name: call-results
inputs.desc: Differential expression or variant data for plotting

inputs.name: network-graph
inputs.desc: Network with module and centrality data

inputs.name: enrichment-results
inputs.desc: Pathway enrichment data for dot plots

outputs.name: figure-set
outputs.desc: Publication-ready figures with captions and source data

outputs.name: figure-legends
outputs.desc: Draft figure legends describing each panel

process: Generate volcano plot of log2 fold change vs. adjusted p-value with labeled top hits
Draw a clustered heatmap of top differentially expressed genes across all samples
Render the network graph with module coloring and hub gene labels
Create enrichment dot plots showing top GO and KEGG terms by gene ratio and significance

steps.description: Package the entire analysis as a reproducible workflow with containerized environments, version-locked tools, and a runnable pipeline definition.

inputs.name: figure-set
inputs.desc: Final analysis outputs to include in the reproducible package

inputs.name: qc-report
inputs.desc: QC data for the methods section

outputs.name: workflow-package
outputs.desc: Snakemake or Nextflow pipeline with Dockerfile and version-locked dependencies

outputs.name: methods-draft
outputs.desc: Draft methods section describing every analysis step, tool, and version

process: Write the pipeline definition (Snakemake or Nextflow) linking every step from QC to figures
Create a Dockerfile or Conda environment file locking every tool and library version
Test the full pipeline from raw reads to final outputs on a clean machine or CI runner
Draft the methods section with tool names, versions, parameters, and database dates

description: Develop a food product from ingredient sourcing through formulation matrix, shelf life testing, sensory evaluation, nutritional analysis, regulatory compliance, and final formulation report.

steps.description: Source ingredients, confirm supplier specifications, and verify regulatory status (GRAS, novel food) for the target market.

inputs.name: product-concept
inputs.desc: Target product type, flavor profile, and nutritional goals

inputs.name: target-market
inputs.desc: Regulatory jurisdiction and consumer segment

outputs.name: ingredient-list
outputs.desc: Approved ingredients with supplier, spec sheet, cost, and regulatory status

outputs.name: allergen-matrix
outputs.desc: Allergen declarations per ingredient and cross-contact risk assessment

process: Define the ingredient functional roles: structure, sweetness, preservation, color, flavor
Source candidates from approved suppliers and collect certificates of analysis
Verify GRAS status or novel food authorization for each ingredient in the target market
Build the allergen matrix and identify cross-contact risks in the supply chain

steps.description: Design a formulation matrix varying key ingredients across a structured experimental space to optimize taste, texture, and stability.

inputs.name: ingredient-list
inputs.desc: Sourced ingredients with specifications

inputs.name: product-concept
inputs.desc: Target sensory and nutritional profile

outputs.name: formulation-matrix
outputs.desc: Table of trial formulations with ingredient percentages and processing parameters

outputs.name: bench-samples
outputs.desc: Prepared prototype samples for evaluation

process: Identify the key variables (sugar level, fat content, hydrocolloid type, pH) and their feasible ranges
Design the trial matrix using mixture design or factorial layout
Prepare bench-top prototypes at lab scale following standardized mixing and processing protocols
Record observations on appearance, viscosity, and immediate taste for each formulation

steps.description: Design and execute accelerated and real-time shelf life studies tracking microbial, chemical, and sensory stability.

inputs.name: bench-samples
inputs.desc: Lead formulation prototypes to test

inputs.name: target-market
inputs.desc: Required shelf life duration and storage conditions

outputs.name: shelf-life-data
outputs.desc: Microbial counts, pH, water activity, color, and sensory scores over time at each condition

outputs.name: shelf-life-estimate
outputs.desc: Predicted shelf life with safety margin and failure mode

process: Set up real-time storage (target conditions) and accelerated storage (elevated temperature/humidity) for each formulation
Pull samples at defined intervals and test: total plate count, yeast/mold, pH, Aw, color, and sensory
Plot degradation curves and identify the shelf-life-limiting parameter
Apply Q10 or Arrhenius modeling to extrapolate from accelerated to real-time shelf life

steps.description: Design and run a sensory evaluation panel: recruit panelists, train on attributes, and score samples using a structured ballot.

inputs.name: bench-samples
inputs.desc: Formulation prototypes for sensory testing

inputs.name: product-concept
inputs.desc: Target sensory profile guiding attribute selection

outputs.name: sensory-scores
outputs.desc: Panelist scores per attribute per sample with statistical analysis

outputs.name: preference-ranking
outputs.desc: Overall preference ranking with significant differences identified

process: Recruit a panel of 8-12 trained assessors or 60+ consumers depending on test type
For descriptive analysis, train panelists on reference standards for each attribute (sweetness, acidity, firmness, etc.)
Present samples in randomized order with three-digit codes using a balanced incomplete block or Williams design
Analyze scores with ANOVA and post-hoc tests, generate spider plots and preference maps

steps.description: Analyze the final formulation for macronutrients, micronutrients, and label-relevant components per regulatory method requirements.

inputs.name: formulation-matrix
inputs.desc: Final formulation with ingredient percentages

inputs.name: target-market
inputs.desc: Regulatory requirements for nutrition labeling

outputs.name: nutrition-panel
outputs.desc: Nutrition facts per serving: calories, fat, carbohydrates, protein, sodium, vitamins, minerals

outputs.name: label-claims
outputs.desc: Permissible nutrient content claims (low-fat, high-fiber, etc.) based on analytical values

process: Calculate theoretical nutrition from ingredient database values as a starting point
Send samples to an accredited lab for proximate analysis (moisture, ash, fat, protein, fiber, carbohydrate by difference)
Analyze micronutrients (vitamins, minerals) relevant to any planned label claims
Round values per FDA or local rounding rules and determine eligible nutrient content claims

steps.description: Verify that the formulation, label, and manufacturing process meet food safety and labeling regulations for the target market.

inputs.name: ingredient-list
inputs.desc: Ingredients with regulatory status

inputs.name: nutrition-panel
inputs.desc: Finalized nutrition facts

inputs.name: allergen-matrix
inputs.desc: Allergen declarations and cross-contact assessment

outputs.name: compliance-checklist
outputs.desc: Regulation-by-regulation compliance status with evidence references

outputs.name: label-draft
outputs.desc: Draft product label with ingredient list, nutrition facts, allergen statement, and required warnings

process: Check each ingredient against the permitted additives list for the target jurisdiction
Verify nutrition label format and rounding against 21 CFR 101 (US) or EU 1169/2011 (EU)
Confirm allergen declaration meets local requirements (FALCPA, EU FIC)
Review label claims, front-of-pack icons, and any required health warnings

steps.description: Compile all development data into the final formulation report with process specification, scale-up notes, and commercialization readiness assessment.

inputs.name: sensory-scores
inputs.desc: Sensory evaluation results

inputs.name: shelf-life-estimate
inputs.desc: Shelf life determination

inputs.name: compliance-checklist
inputs.desc: Regulatory compliance status

outputs.name: formulation-report
outputs.desc: Complete product development report with formulation, process, stability, sensory, nutrition, and regulatory sections

outputs.name: scale-up-protocol
outputs.desc: Pilot plant process parameters and critical control points for scale-up

process: Compile the formulation with exact ingredient percentages, water activity, and pH targets
Document the process flow from batching through filling with time, temperature, and shear specifications
Summarize shelf life, sensory, and regulatory findings with pass/fail against acceptance criteria
Outline scale-up considerations: equipment, batch size, mixing time adjustments, and HACCP plan

description: Run a quantum computing investigation from qubit characterization through gate calibration, circuit design, noise modeling, error mitigation, benchmarking, and fidelity analysis.

steps.description: Characterize qubit parameters: T1, T2, readout fidelity, frequency, and anharmonicity for each qubit on the device.

inputs.name: device-spec
inputs.desc: Quantum processor model, qubit count, and connectivity map

inputs.name: characterization-targets
inputs.desc: Qubits to characterize and parameters of interest

outputs.name: qubit-parameters
outputs.desc: T1, T2, readout fidelity, frequency, and anharmonicity per qubit

outputs.name: qubit-ranking
outputs.desc: Qubits ranked by coherence and readout quality for circuit assignment

process: Run T1 relaxation experiments on each qubit and fit exponential decay
Run Ramsey and echo experiments to measure T2* and T2 (Hahn echo) decoherence times
Measure single-shot readout fidelity and assignment error matrix
Rank qubits by composite quality metric (T1, T2, readout fidelity) for circuit planning

steps.description: Calibrate single-qubit and two-qubit gates to minimize error rates, verified by randomized benchmarking.

inputs.name: qubit-parameters
inputs.desc: Coherence and frequency data for the target qubits

inputs.name: gate-set
inputs.desc: Gates to calibrate (single-qubit rotations, CNOT or CZ)

outputs.name: calibrated-gates
outputs.desc: Gate pulse parameters (amplitude, duration, frequency, drag coefficient) per gate

outputs.name: gate-error-rates
outputs.desc: Single-qubit and two-qubit error rates from randomized benchmarking

process: Optimize single-qubit gate pulses using DRAG calibration to suppress leakage
Calibrate two-qubit gates (cross-resonance or controlled-Z) and tune up conditional phase
Run single-qubit and interleaved randomized benchmarking to measure gate error rates
Iterate calibration if error rates exceed the target threshold

steps.description: Design the quantum circuit for the target algorithm, transpile to the native gate set, and optimize circuit depth.

inputs.name: algorithm-spec
inputs.desc: Algorithm or experiment to implement (VQE, QAOA, Grover, simulation, etc.)

inputs.name: calibrated-gates
inputs.desc: Available native gate set and connectivity

inputs.name: qubit-ranking
inputs.desc: Best qubits for circuit assignment

outputs.name: transpiled-circuit
outputs.desc: Circuit transpiled to native gates with qubit mapping and depth statistics

outputs.name: circuit-metrics
outputs.desc: Gate count, circuit depth, CNOT count, and estimated success probability

process: Implement the target algorithm in an abstract circuit representation
Transpile to the native gate set using connectivity-aware routing and optimization passes
Map logical qubits to physical qubits using the quality ranking to minimize error impact
Report final gate count, CNOT count, circuit depth, and estimated success probability

steps.description: Build a noise model of the device from characterization data for use in simulation and error mitigation design.

inputs.name: qubit-parameters
inputs.desc: T1, T2, and readout error data

inputs.name: gate-error-rates
inputs.desc: Per-gate error rates from benchmarking

outputs.name: noise-model
outputs.desc: Calibrated noise model (depolarizing, thermal relaxation, readout) for the device

outputs.name: simulated-baseline
outputs.desc: Noisy simulation results for comparison with hardware runs

process: Construct per-qubit thermal relaxation channels from T1 and T2 data
Add depolarizing noise to each gate calibrated to measured error rates
Include readout error using the measured assignment matrix
Run the transpiled circuit on the noisy simulator to establish the baseline expectation

steps.description: Select and configure error mitigation techniques (ZNE, PEC, measurement error mitigation) suited to the circuit and noise profile.

inputs.name: noise-model
inputs.desc: Calibrated noise model identifying dominant error channels

inputs.name: transpiled-circuit
inputs.desc: Circuit to be mitigated

outputs.name: mitigation-strategy
outputs.desc: Selected mitigation methods with configuration parameters

outputs.name: overhead-estimate
outputs.desc: Additional circuit executions or classical compute required per method

process: Evaluate applicability of zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) based on circuit depth and noise structure
Assess probabilistic error cancellation (PEC) feasibility given the gate noise characterization
Configure measurement error mitigation using the readout assignment matrix
Estimate the shot overhead and classical post-processing cost for the chosen strategy

steps.description: Execute the circuit on hardware with and without error mitigation, collecting sufficient shots for statistical analysis.

inputs.name: transpiled-circuit
inputs.desc: Circuit ready for execution

inputs.name: mitigation-strategy
inputs.desc: Error mitigation configuration to apply

outputs.name: raw-counts
outputs.desc: Measurement outcome distributions for unmitigated and mitigated runs

outputs.name: execution-metadata
outputs.desc: Timestamps, shot counts, device calibration snapshot, and job IDs

process: Submit the unmitigated circuit for the baseline shot count
Submit the mitigated circuit variants (noise-scaled, etc.) with the required additional shots
Record device calibration data at execution time for reproducibility
Verify that result distributions pass basic sanity checks (bitstring format, total counts)

steps.description: Analyze execution results: compute expectation values, compare hardware to ideal and noisy simulation, assess error mitigation effectiveness, and report fidelity.

inputs.name: raw-counts
inputs.desc: Hardware measurement results, mitigated and unmitigated

inputs.name: simulated-baseline
inputs.desc: Noisy and ideal simulation results for comparison

outputs.name: fidelity-report
outputs.desc: Expectation values, fidelity metrics, and error mitigation improvement factor

outputs.name: experiment-summary
outputs.desc: Full experiment report: device, circuit, noise model, mitigation, and results with reproducibility notes

process: Compute expectation values and confidence intervals from the raw count distributions
Calculate fidelity metrics (Hellinger fidelity, state fidelity) against the ideal simulation
Quantify the improvement from error mitigation by comparing mitigated vs. unmitigated fidelity
Write the experiment summary with all parameters, results, and instructions for reproduction
